subject: Merging data imputed datasets by imputation number and ID

messages.author: 7c61453ccc67f9a0
messages.subject: Merging data imputed datasets by imputation number and ID
parts:
Hi,

I want to test the model in Data Analysis Example 1, Chapter 9 of Enders (2010) “Applied Missing Data Analysis.”  It is a simple regression model with an interaction effect (gender moderates the effect of well-being on job performance).  Enders recommends imputing the values of the two groups (males and females) separately to preserve the gender specific means and covariances.  I have done this using Amelia.  But now I need to merge the two sets of imputed data sets in a way that can be read by lavaan (runMI).   The imputations datasets are *named* (imputation 1 through imputation 5, as I have set m = 5 for now), but I don’t know how to use this information to merge dataset 1 for females with dataset 1 for males, dataset 2 for females with dataset 2 for males, and so on.  It is not the same as merging files by variables internal to the dataset (there is no imputation_ID in the data).  I could add such an ID to each dataset, but this would be incredibly burdensome if I wanted 50 imputed data sets.  As far as I can see, ameliabind does not merge datasets (there is no “by” command on which to combine two dataset).  So, does anyone have a reference for how to merge imputed datasets while maintaining the infrastructure used by Amelia and readable by lavaan?

Thanks,

Bill Cook

PS:     I know I could conduct the regression analysis and test the interaction effect using a multiple groups SEM, but that seems inefficient, and I envision other applications where this would not be a solution (e.g., imputing the scores of husbands and wives in an APIM dyadic data analysis).

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Merging data imputed datasets by imputation number and ID
parts:
If I understand correctly, you have 2 different Amelia objects, one for each sex.  They don't contain the same people/observations, so you don't really need to merge the data by any variables, you just need to stack them.  I assume the imputed data sets for each sex have the same column names in the same order, and that you have included the sex indicator in the "id" argument in amelia(..., id = "sex", ...) so that this variable is still included in the imputed data sets even though it is not used in the imputation model.  You can use the same type of loop in the mi.meld() example to create a list of stack data sets:

nImps <- 5
maleImputations <- amelia(maleData, n = nImps, id = "sex", ...)
female Imputations <- amelia(femaleData, n = nImps, id = "sex", ...)

## create an empty list to populate
stackedImps <- list(NULL)

## populate the list in a loop
for (i in 1:nImps) {
  stackedImps[[i]] <- rbind(maleImputations$imputations[[i]], femaleImputations$imputations[[i]])
}

Then you can feed the stackedImps list as the data argument to runMI()

FYI, you can also include sex as the cross-sectional variable in amelia(..., cs = "sex", ...), but it isn't the same as Enders' (2010) example.

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Merging data imputed datasets by imputation number and ID
parts:
Hi Bill,

There are no problems with your model specification or your call to Amelia.  The reason you see the warnings is because it is a saturated model.  Saturated models have a chi-squared value of zero, which is all well and good, but they also have zero degrees of freedom.  So when runMI() tries to combine the chi-squared values, it is making a call to calculate the probabilities (p values) of observing the chi-squared or F value when df = 0, which is undefined.  However, notice that all the warnings concern calls to pf() and pchisq(), so that is the only issue.  You models were estimated and parameters combined successfully:

> summary(out.mi, standardized = TRUE)
lavaan (0.5-12) converged normally after   5 iterations

  Number of observations                           480

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               -0.000
  Degrees of freedom                                 0
  P-value (Chi-square)                           1.000

Parameter estimates:

  Information                                 Expected
  Standard Errors                             Standard

                   Estimate  Std.err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
Regressions:
  performance ~
    female           -2.300    0.570   -4.035    0.000   -2.300   -0.914
    wb_c              0.339    0.061    5.570    0.000    0.339    0.317
    g_wb              0.338    0.089    3.783    0.000    0.338    0.888

Variances:
    performance       1.202    0.080                      1.202    0.765

I'll see if the author of runMI() minds putting in a logical check for df = 0, to skip the combination of chi-squared statistics in that situation so that these false alarms won't show up.

Terry

Agreed. And adding the option chi="none" gets rid of all the warnings:

out.mi <- runMI(employReg3, data=mf_merge$imputations, fun="sem",
chi="none")

automatically... and that is why I CCed this to Sunthud ;-)

Yves.

I just pushed a fix in github to prevent pf() and pchisq() from being called when df == 0, just returning a p-value of 1 in that case.  It wasn't in time for it to be in the update semTools 0.4-0 that was just released (which includes really cool new tools), but it will be in the next update.  However, I think Yves' fix is more parsimonious than mine, and it would cut down on run time because there would be no calculations to combine chi-squared values at all.  So I'll make that change, and it should be active in semTools 0.4-1.  Either way, users will be able to just use the default runMI(..., chi = "all") without getting false alarms.

Thanks for the suggestion,

Terry
